revision_log.author: Elenchos
revision_log.why: Executes section 1.3.3 of the A2 MSSP core agreed 3/3 at sha256 8656A872133D826CF0E08B7AFAE3EFDBAC0A83F6CCB427F507F38B6681D2D05F. Both corrections were reported by the outsourced A1 implementer reading this file from outside; neither was found by the three architects.

The stack entry was written before implementation and A1 measured a textarea carrying all four editing capabilities on Windows. Nothing checked implementation against stack, which is why the divergence survived three days.

capability_acceptance_map['document-state']: 'steps 2 and 6' -> the row now names an assertion that can fail while text-view-edit stays green. The old row rested on the same workflow steps as text-view-edit and asserted nothing of its own, so one piece of evidence was counted twice in an 11-capability denominator.

target_platform.note: One measured target. Nothing here implies cross-platform support.

stack.acceptance_runs_against: the packaged executable, never a dev server
stack.playwright_electron_status: official docs mark Electron automation experimental; the version used goes into the evidence, and if an upgrade breaks it that is reported as an integration failure rather than fixed by changing the acceptance

primary_workflow: create a new empty document and type into it
save it with Save As to a new path
select text, cut it, and paste it back
open a pinned UTF-8 fixture from disk
find and replace within the document
close the application, relaunch it, and manually reopen the file
an EXTERNAL oracle verifies the saved bytes and line endings against the expected value
why_external_oracle: The program must not be its own oracle. Bytes it wrote being equal to bytes it reads back is a statement about one program, not about correctness.

capability_acceptance_map.ui-shell: every workflow step is driven through it; a step needing an internal call fails ui_complete
capability_acceptance_map.error-report: attack: the invalid-not-utf8 fixture is refused BY NAME and the name reaches the GUI
capability_acceptance_map.document-io: steps 5 and 9 - reading and writing the user's document
capability_acceptance_map.document-state: steps 2 and 6 - after edit, undo, redo and save, the visible dirty projection equals the main-process authoritative dirty state; this assertion can fail while typed text remains visible
capability_acceptance_map.text-view-edit: steps 2 and 6 - what is typed is what is shown
capability_acceptance_map.encoding-eol: step 11 - external oracle checks bytes and line endings across LF, CRLF and BOM fixtures
capability_acceptance_map.unsaved-change-guard: attack: close with unsaved changes by a route the acceptance does not drive

capability_acceptance_rule: Every capability maps to a DISTINCT failable row. No row may be cited by two capabilities without an independent assertion, and a capability with no row may not be in the denominator.
fixture_policy: Pinned by hash before implementation. The 1 MiB fixture exists to stop tiny-fixture laundering, not to support a latency claim.

encoding_policy.read: UTF-8 only; anything else is refused by name, never guessed
encoding_policy.bom: a UTF-8 BOM present on read is preserved on write
encoding_policy.eol: the file's existing line endings are preserved; a new document uses LF

timing_policy.why_notmeasured: a second-count verdict without pinned CPU, RAM, storage and background load is false precision
timing_policy.recorded: reference machine facts and raw launch/open/find/save timings, as data only
timing_policy.not_claimed: fast, responsive, or any cross-machine latency verdict

schedule_reporting.removed: the phrase 'materially longer than nine days' from v1 - a movable success word replaced by recorded events

implementation_slices.name: file loop
implementation_slices.covers: packaged launch, new/open/edit/Save As/save, unsaved-change guard, manual reopen, external byte and EOL oracle

implementation_slices.name: boundary loop
implementation_slices.covers: UTF-8/BOM/EOL policy, named GUI refusal of invalid encoding, full regression and packaging evidence

slice_rule: Each slice starts RED with contract and GUI tests before any production code. The final denominator does not change because of implementation order.

comparator.mssp_candidate: FMS/SCL/SMS/TMS/DMS split with declared contracts and no sibling imports
comparator.ordinary_alternative: one module with a conventional component split, no capability registry, no declared contracts
comparator.same_dependencies: the ordinary alternative is costed with the SAME Electron and editor-component versions, so a dependency choice is never misattributed to MSSP
comparator.mssp_effect_verdict: unknown by construction - only one arm is built

topology.hypothesis: each domain capability may become one TMS unit
topology.falsification: a unit with no state of its own, exactly one caller, and no ability to be exercised alone by the island test is evidence the hypothesis was wrong for that capability
topology.on_falsification: append a revision merging or moving it; do not keep a thin file to protect the shape

external_provider_contract.rule: the editor component supplies or influences document state, selection, history, clipboard and search. Using it is legitimate; crediting it to MSSP is not.
external_provider_contract.excluded_from_numerator: Electron, the editor component and Playwright themselves never count toward any local or shared MSSP foundation
external_provider_contract.thin_wrapper_rule: a TMS that is only a one-caller no-state wrapper over an editor-component or browser API triggers module-splitting; naming it a capability does not make it an architectural result

electron_security_boundary.content: local packaged content only; no runtime remote code or navigation
electron_security_boundary.filesystem: reachable only through a minimal preload/contextBridge API; raw ipcRenderer is never exposed
electron_security_boundary.ipc: sender and arguments validated in the main process
electron_security_boundary.paths: Open and Save paths normalised and validated in the main process; non-UTF-8 refusal is returned to the UI without giving the renderer Node fs access

dialog_coverage.automated: packaged-app GUI automation supplies pinned dialog paths from the main process in test mode; the report is marked dialog_path=stubbed
dialog_coverage.native_smoke: a separate Windows smoke exercises the real Open and Save As dialogs and is its own artifact
dialog_coverage.rule: the automated path may never be reported as native-dialog coverage

membership.policy: role-scoped, append-only, effective from a commit. Independence keys on implementation_builder for the product tree only.
membership.self_declared_only: each party declares their own roles; I author only my own row
membership.release_gate: at least one independent attack pass by a party that is not an implementation_builder of the FINAL product tree digest
membership.role_change: a reviewer who edits production code joins implementation_builder from that commit, and the final product needs another independent pass

slice_specific: unsaved-change guard bypassed by a route the acceptance does not drive
invalid encoding must be refused by name, not silently mangled
undo across a save point must not lose the dirty state
reopened file byte-identical including line endings
tiny-fixture laundering: the 1 MiB fixture must be exercised, not only the small ones

how_this_slice_could_come_out_badly: the GUI cannot complete one of the nine domain capabilities without an internal call, and ui_complete fails
the reopened file is not byte-identical and the external oracle rejects it
a capability turns out to be a thin editor-component wrapper, which is module-splitting done to myself
the acceptance can only drive stubbed dialogs, so native-dialog coverage stays NotMeasured and must be reported as such
a capability in capability_acceptance_map has no observable step that can actually fail, which would make the map decoration
stop_boundary: No A2 production until all of: a unified source baseline containing both the A1 head and the A0 boundary head; this preregistration green under its own fail-closed verifier with the append-only history intact; an exact workbench request derived from the three-architect-agreed core digest without broadening it; and Neo's explicit authorization to send that request. Three-architect agreement on the core is not by itself send authorization. This boundary grants no merge to main, no deployment, and no MSSP method adoption.

revision_log_schemas.why: Both shapes exist in the history. A row matching neither, or matching one with a required field missing, is a defect: it renders as literal `undefined` and no check noticed until a reader saw the built page.
